ledger.claim: The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is met on identification: the trip record (EV-TRIP-00310), the GPS trace (EV-GPS-00310) and the fare breakdown (EV-FARE-00310) all carry trip_id TRP-00310 and the same 2026-08-12 morning window (pickup 08:15-08:20, dropoff 08:46), so the artifacts describe one and the same trip and nothing in this case turns on a mismatched or missing record.

The $3.00 CTE (Braddell Rd towards City) gantry line on the receipt is a phantom. Its coordinates (1.3418, 103.8489) sit 5,551 m from the nearest GPS fix in the trace - more than twenty times the 250 m radius POL-RD-09(4) uses to treat a fix as a crossing - and the fare breakdown itself flags the line on_optimal_route false, while the booked optimal route is ECP then Nicoll Hwy. Under POL-RD-09(4) a charge line for a gantry the gps_trace never passes is a billing-integrity failure, refunded in full as a standalone correction, available whether or not a deviation exists.

The other half of the ERP total is sound and the rider does not contest it: the ECP (Fort Rd) $2.00 line is matched at 0 m from fix index 54 at 08:29:25 and lies on the optimal route, and the trip record's optimal_route_erp_sgd is $2.00. The receipt therefore overstates ERP by exactly the $3.00 CTE line, so the correction due on ERP is $3.00, not the $5.00 the rider's receipt shows.

The driver's answer that 'ERP is automatic from the IU, I cannot control it' is no answer to this line. POL-RD-09(4) makes a gantry charge the gps_trace never passes refundable as a billing-integrity correction irrespective of cause or fault and irrespective of who set the IU; the vehicle did not cross the Braddell gantry and the rider should not pay for it.

The rider's second head of claim - that the driver took a longer way - does not survive the trace, and the rider does not press it. The trace governs under POL-RD-01 and records 13.7 km against a booked optimal of 13.0 km: an excess of 0.7 km and 5.38%, below both the 0.8 km absolute test and the 20% relative test, so no deviation is established and no distance-or-time refund arises on this record. Only the POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity correction survives.

The bundle holds no traffic advisory covering this trip window: EV-ADVIS-00310-01 is MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT - a citable absence. No external traffic event can therefore be invoked on this record to explain either the measured route or the charged gantry, and the unimpaired 157-fix trace (coverage 100%, no gaps, max gap 0 s) stands as the only account of where the vehicle went.

The rider's central allegation — that the driver took a longer way than needed — fails the POL-RD-01 gate on this trip's own trace. The derived deviation block measures the excess at 0.70 km against an optimal of 13.0 km, i.e. 5.38%. Both establishment tests must pass and neither does: 0.70 km is below the 0.8 km absolute threshold, and 5.38% is below the 20% proportional threshold. Where the trace figure and the trip record disagree the trace governs; here they agree (13.7 km both), so there is no straddle to exploit. No deviation exists, and the routing part of the claim stands or falls as NO_ACTION.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and has not discharged it: the artifacts describe one trip (matching trip_id TRP-00310 across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown), but the second limb — an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold, measured from an unimpaired trace — cannot be shown, because the trace is unimpaired and shows only 5.38% / 0.70 km. With no threshold-meeting excess, no burden shifts to the driver and the rider's uncited suspicion that the route was longer carries no weight.

The driver's own statement — 'Route was normal ECP' — is corroborated, not contradicted, by the artifacts. The platform's booked optimal route is recorded as 'ECP then Nicoll Hwy' with an optimal-route ERP of $2.00, and the ECP (Fort Rd towards City) gantry the driver crossed is flagged on_optimal_route true with the nearest trace fix 0 m from it. The driver drove the corridor the platform itself selected at booking.

Because no deviation is established under POL-RD-01, POL-RD-02 does not run and no distance-or-time refund is available to the rider. The recomputation the fare ledger carries — recomputed_fare 19.67 against a charged_total of 25.16, a refund of 5.49 (5.50 rounded) — presupposes an established deviation and is not payable on this record. The fare model is METERED, so POL-RD-11 does not apply and opens no alternative route to a distance refund either.

There is no repeat-deviation pattern to weigh against the driver. Under POL-RD-06 the citable counters are driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d and driver_profile.completed_trips_90d: the driver's trailing-90-day figure is 0 against 260 completed trips, below both limbs of the test, and in any event no MATERIAL deviation exists on this trip to trigger the clause. The lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter is context only under POL-GEN-01 and is not the field POL-RD-06 names.

ledger.claim: No POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fires on this record. The trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown; the trace runs at a 10 s cadence with 157 fixes over 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds, so it is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c) and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged; and the only charge line without a trace counterpart is the CTE line, which is refunded under POL-RD-09(4) and is expressly carved out of POL-RD-10(8). The case is decidable without escalation.

The ECP (Fort Rd towards City) charge of $2.00 stands and is not refundable as a standalone correction under POL-RD-09(4). That gantry carries coordinates, is matched by a trace fix at 0 m — far inside the 250 m crossing radius — and is flagged on_optimal_route true, so it is a properly chargeable on-route pass-through. The rider's own premise that the ECP gantry is $2.00 is in fact satisfied by the ledger, which charges exactly $2.00 for it.

Conceded: the CTE (Braddell Rd towards City) line of $3.00 is not matched by the trace — the closest the vehicle came to that gantry was 5,551 m, far outside the 250 m match radius — so the rider is right that the trip never went near Braddell, and that line falls to be refunded in full as a standalone billing-integrity correction under POL-RD-09(4). But it is a $3.00 pass-through correction for a phantom gantry on a complete, unimpaired trace, not a route-deviation refund, and it does not carry with it the distance-and-time refund the rider also asks for.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: this case turns on two questions — was the route longer than it should have been, and is the ERP on the receipt right.

1) The route. Under POL-RD-01 the GPS trace (EV-GPS-00310) governs distance. It records 13.7 km against a booked optimal of 13.0 km — an excess of 0.7 km, or 5.4%. Both establishment tests must pass and neither does: 0.7 km is below the 0.8 km absolute threshold and 5.4% is below the 20% relative threshold. No deviation is established, so POL-RD-02 does not run and no distance-or-time refund is available. The driver's account that the route was normal ECP is consistent with the record: EV-TRIP-00310 states the booked optimal was 'ECP then Nicoll Hwy', and the ECP gantry crossed is flagged on the optimal route. Accordingly the rider's 'longer way' head of claim is rejected and POL-RD-11 is not reached (the fare model is METERED).

2) The ERP. Of the $5.00 charged, $2.00 is the ECP (Fort Rd towards City) gantry. That line is matched by a trace fix at 0 m — well inside the 250 m crossing radius POL-RD-09(4) uses — and lies on the optimal route, so it is a properly chargeable pass-through and stands. The rider is right that this gantry should be $2.00, and the ledger charges exactly $2.00. The other $3.00 is the CTE (Braddell Rd towards City) line. The nearest the vehicle ever came to that gantry was 5,551 m, more than twenty times the match radius, so the trace never crosses it. Under POL-RD-09(4) a charge line for a gantry the trace never passes is a billing-integrity failure and is refunded in full as a standalone correction, available whether or not a deviation exists. The driver's point that the IU charges automatically does not change this: the correction is not fault-based, the vehicle simply did not cross that gantry. This $3.00 is a pass-through correction only; it does not carry the distance-and-time refund the rider also asked for.

Money: charged_total $25.16; ERP charged $5.00 ($2.00 ECP + $3.00 CTE); refund $3.00 of the $8.00 contested, rounded up to the nearest $0.05 (already on the grid). No driver compensation is due: distance_charged_km (13.7) equals the trace distance, so there is no unbilled shortfall for POL-RD-04.

No POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fires. The trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown; the trace is unimpaired under POL-RD-07(a)-(c) (157 fixes, 10 s cadence, 100% coverage, no gaps, maximum gap 0 s); and the only charge line without a trace counterpart is the CTE line, refunded under POL-RD-09(4) and expressly carved out of POL-RD-10(8). The bundle holds no traffic advisory for this trip (EV-ADVIS-00310-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT); that absence is itself citable but carries no fact, and since no party asserts an external traffic cause nothing turns on it. The driver's citable 90-day counters show no repeat-deviation pattern (deviation_flags_90d 0 against 260 completed trips) and there is no material deviation in any event, so POL-RD-06 produces no uplift and no conduct referral; the lifetime prior_deviation_flags figure is context only under POL-GEN-01 and was not used.

Confidence 0.90: every fact the ruling rests on is carried by artifacts at weight 1.0 (EV-GPS-00310, EV-TRIP-00310, EV-FARE-00310), so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0. The monetary effect ($3.00) does not exceed the $8.00 execution threshold and may be executed automatically, subject to appeal under POL-GEN-04.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
referrals: POL-RD-09(4): billing-integrity finding — the $3.00 CTE (Braddell Rd towards City) gantry line on EV-FARE-00310 was charged although the trace (EV-GPS-00310) never came within 250 m of that gantry (nearest fix 5,551 m); refunded in full as a standalone pass-through correction and recorded for billing-integrity review.
